runs.text: Tandem is a project with several epics (ui, core, cli, mcp, and more) but the board funnels almost everything through one Tandem lane plus leftovers (Retro, Port, tandem-ui, Hosting). Triage, ownership, and the app and CLI journeys around lanes (create, list, move, draw a batch) are messy as a result: it is unclear where an epic lives, how a batch draws from it, and what the user clicks or types to work an epic end to end.

Define the epic lane set for the tandem project (ui, core, cli, mcp, plus whatever else the pass finds in the tree: rust core, app shell, renderer, skills, docs) with one line each on what lives there and what does not. Retire or remap the confusing overlaps (Tandem vs tandem-ui vs Port) with an explicit move map, no silent drops.

Make the journey functional end to end: lane create/list/move in CLI and app, ticket move across lanes, batch draw from one epic lane, sprint open/run/close naming the lane, with errors that name the lane and the fix.

Migrate the current open Tandem rows to their epic lanes per the map, with a dated comment on each moved ticket naming the old lane and the reason. Parked rows (on-hold/human) keep their hold and owner across the move.
Cover at the seam: store/domain tests for lane CRUD and moves, CLI tests for the lane verbs, app tests for the lane faces touched. One command per suite touched, scoped runs before the PR.

The epic lanes exist, the open Tandem rows sit in the epic lane that owns them, and a cold pass can create a lane, move a ticket, draw a batch, and open/run/close a sprint in an epic lane from both CLI and app with no mess.
CI green on the head; the PR names the lane map, the moved rows, and the filtered test commands run locally.
Renaming the project or touching other projects lanes (code-rank, Hosting): tandem epics only.
Auto-sorting rules or WIP limits: placement is explicit, no magic.
